$comment:
Currency facts. Volatility is `slow`, not `stable`: currencies change — Zimbabwe has changed twice in five years, which is why it is absent here rather than present and wrong.

`names` is the FULL form ("Indian rupee", not "rupee") because that is the sourced, cross-checkable name of the thing, and it is what the country and collection screens show. `shortNames` is what a QUESTION uses, and it exists because the full form hands the answer over in both directions: "Which country uses the Indian rupee?" is answered by anybody who can read, and "What money do people use in India?" offered against Nepalese rupee and Bangladeshi taka is the same question wearing a hat. Fifty-four of the sixty-four values in this pack shared a stem with their own country's name in at least one shipped locale — this was not an edge case, it was most of the attribute. (The ten euro rows are the remainder, and the sixty-fifth currency-attribute fact in the geography pack is geo.ZW.currency, which lives in facts.sensitive-examples.v1.json and is quizzable:false.)

Dropping the demonym also makes the reverse question honest rather than merely hard: "rupee" belongs to India, Pakistan and Nepal alike, so isAmbiguous refuses it, the same way it already refused the euro's ten members and the CFA franc's two. What survives — forint, quetzal, pula, kina — are the currencies whose short name really does name one country. See isAmbiguous and displayValue in packages/engines/src/content.

The euro carries no short form: its name is already the short one.

No new claim is made here. Each short name is the head noun of the full name in the same source cited on the item — the Wikipedia article "Indian rupee" is about the rupee — so `pnpm content:crosscheck`, which compares `names.en` against world-countries, is unaffected and still checks the sourced value.
